1.why: Reset verify compares the supplied token only to session.reset.token, which was issued with a bound accountId for that session.

2.why: The reset token lives only on the issuing session and must match that session’s reset record, so it does not work for another user’s session.

3.why: password/change marks the reset used and clears recovery flags but never invalidates other sessions’ authenticatedAccountId values.

4.why: Bun.serve is started with TLS cert/key on 3443 and plain HTTP on 3000 permanently redirects to HTTPS with HSTS set.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but reset tokens and MFA codes are stored/returned as plaintext secrets in session memory rather than encrypted.

6.why: No real email body is built from user input; responses use a generic message and logs avoid account detail, though mock tokens are exposed in-session for the demo.

7.why: Emails are normalizeEmail-validated, passwords go through validPassword, bodies are JSON-parsed objects, and client UI uses textContent.

8.why: Redirects are fixed to https://localhost and client navigation only uses hard-coded same-origin paths with no user-controlled URL.

9.why: There are no email templates that embed user-supplied HTML or scripts; delivery is only simulated server-side.

10.why: Error JSON is generic, but recovery/status and the client Logs deliberately surface mockDeliveryToken and MFA codes.

11.why: The demo account’s bcrypt password hash is hard-coded in source; runtime secrets are only in memory, not absent from the codebase entirely.

12.why: A single demo account with a fixed precomputed password hash is embedded and is the only login target, i.e. default demo credentials.

13.why: isAllowed/failure enforce per-session and global attempt windows with lockouts on login, reset-verify, and MFA verify.

14.why: recovery/request always returns the same generic ‘If an eligible account matches…’ message whether or not the email exists.

15.why: Reset tokens are randomBytes(32) base64url values bound to session.reset.accountId and checked as user/session-specific.
